q7.answer: Not decided. The draft says engines only read billing_mode from the config service and that a flip waits until no charge is unknown, with ownership recorded per period and changed only at a flip with no period in flight. It does not say how workers learn of a change (polling or push) or what a worker does with an invoice it is computing when the mode changes.

q8.answer: Gate evidence is kept in two places: the versioned rollout record next to billing_mode holds the streak, invoice counts, the 14-day count, Finance sign-off and the new_only timestamp, and the nightly comparison store holds one row per day per customer set. A person makes every forward move, the controller refuses it while the gate reads fail, and the flag and record change together under compare-and-set so a mode never changes without its gate state.

q9.answer: Not decided. The draft specifies only that the 2 percent rule over any 10-minute window starts Rollback at Fence in both or new_only. It does not name the component that watches the rate, and the minimum attempt count and whether unknown-outcome charges count as failures are still open (question 4).

q10.answer: Once Fence stops the new engine, no new charges start, and due periods wait. Reconcile identifies the due, unbilled periods, and the old engine charges them only after Flip writes billing_mode as old_only, with any period whose charge is still unknown held at Drain and not handed over.

q11.answer: Each charge carries an idempotency key that is checked before every charge, and the ledger is the record of what was charged. Reconcile compares ledger against provider so already-billed periods are excluded before the flip, unknown outcomes are looked up by key and never retried under a new key, and at most one engine may charge a given period.

q12.answer: The rollout record stores the last completed step, and every step is idempotent. A crash or a Hold (from Drain, Reconcile or Reprocess) leaves the rollout paused with billing_mode unchanged and the new engine fenced, and on-call resumes from Fence to re-run the steps.
